# hamcrest-matcher-generator

> hamcrest-matcher-generator is a Java annotation processor (Java 17+, Kotlin supported). At compile time it generates, for the model classes you configure, a Hamcrest matcher (`XMatcher` with `isX()`) and an AssertJ assertion (`XAssert` with `assertThat(x)`). Generated code carries no license of this project, so it is yours to use.

The library is published on Maven Central as `io.github.marmer.testutils:hamcrest-matcher-generator` (Hamcrest backend) and `io.github.marmer.testutils:assertj-assertion-generator` (AssertJ backend). Both are annotation processors that read one `@GenerateMatchers` configuration annotation, and both need Java 17 or newer to run.

Typical usage: add the generator to the test classpath and the annotation processor path, put `@GenerateMatchers("your.model.package")` on any class, then write `assertThat(customer, isCustomer().withName("Ada"))` (Hamcrest) or `CustomerAssert.assertThat(customer).hasName("Ada")` (AssertJ). The completeness check (`checkingAllProperties()`, `hasAllPropertiesChecked()`) fails a test when a property was neither checked nor ignored.

## User guide

- [Getting started](${docs.base.url}guide/getting-started.html): Maven dependencies, the processor path, the configuration annotation and a first test.
- [Configuration](${docs.base.url}guide/configuration.html): selecting and excluding types with packages and class names, the package of the generated types.
- [Hamcrest backend](${docs.base.url}guide/hamcrest-backend.html): the generated matcher API (`withX`, `resetX`, `ignoringX`, `checkingAllProperties()`, `isXLike(reference)` and its `equals` fallback for types outside the round).
- [AssertJ backend](${docs.base.url}guide/assertj-backend.html): the generated assertion API (`hasX`, `hasXSatisfying`, `isX`, `hasAllPropertiesChecked()`), the assertion path, files written once per package, clashing class names and `usingRecursiveComparison()` for the whole object.
- [Completeness check](${docs.base.url}guide/completeness-check.html): the opt-in check that fails when a property was neither checked nor ignored, with `checkingAllProperties()`, `hasAllPropertiesChecked()`, `ignoringX()` and the Kotlin DSL.
- [Mismatch messages](${docs.base.url}guide/mismatch-messages.html): how a failed matcher or assertion names the property path, nested, in collections and in the completeness check, with real golden messages.
- [Kotlin](${docs.base.url}guide/kotlin.html): KAPT setup and its source directories, Kotlin property names and nullability, the generated Kotlin DSL with its Kotlin 1.9 language level, and IntelliJ with Kotlin tests.
- [IDE setup](${docs.base.url}guide/ide-setup.html): making Eclipse, IntelliJ IDEA and other IDEs see the generated sources.
- [Migrating from 5.x](${docs.base.url}guide/migration.html): Java 11 users stay on 5.x, the new coordinates and bridge jars, `@GenerateMatchers` with the deprecated `@MatcherConfiguration` alias, the new package of `BeanPropertyMatcher`, `javax.annotation` and the opt-in features.
- [Architecture](${docs.base.url}guide/architecture.html): where the architecture documentation is.

## Architecture

- [Architecture documentation (arc42)](${docs.base.url}architecture/index.html): context, building blocks, runtime view of one generation round, deployment and architecture decisions, with C4 views.
